problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨4t,3{t}^{2}-1⟩\,,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position  $r=⟨-2,0⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the times when the particle is at the origin.

choices.value: The particle is never at the origin

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨8(1+2t)^{3},\,4t⟩,\,t\in (0,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨1,\,-2⟩$ when $t=0,$ find the times when the particle intersects the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

The particle intersects the $x$-axis when $t=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle intersects the $x$-axis when its position is $r=⟨x,0⟩,$ where $x$ is arbitrary. So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨8(1+2t)^{3},\,4t⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 8(1+2t)^{3}\,\text{d}t,\,\int 4t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨(1+2t)^{4}+{C}_{1},\,2{t}^{2}+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨1,-2⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨(1+0)^{4}+{C}_{1},\,2(0)^{2}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,-2⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=-2.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(1+2t)^{4},\,2{t}^{2}-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the times when the particle intersects the $x$-axis, we solve for the times at which the $y$-coordinate of the position vector is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 2(t-1)(t+1) & =0 \\ t & =1,-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t$ must be positive, we conclude that the particle intersects the $x$-axis when $t=1.$
